result.topic_en: Notes on a Gaussian-integer analogue of Eisenstein's lattice-point (bracket/floor function) argument for biquadratic reciprocity: sums of bracket symbols over residues modulo a complex prime, a lattice diagram labelled by residues 0–3, and the values of [2ξ]−2[ξ] and [2η]−2[η].

methods.what: Decomposition of a bracket symbol [p,p'] into a sum of four bracket terms involving multiples of the modulus P (lattice-point path decomposition)
Expressing the bracket as a sum over least residues α modulo P of brackets of α + p/P, α + p'/P
Condition on the residue system: α/P = ξ+iη with ξ, η in (0,1)

Areas/probabilities of the four quarters of the unit square with split point (α,β)

items.english: The individual α must be such that, setting α/P = ξ+iη, ξ and η are positive and less than 1.
